text:
alejandro: noticing a p99 jump on pool-prod-gpu-5 starting ~09:10 UTC, tokens/ms halved for small-sequence traffic (seq=8). seeing big tail but throughput steady. any recent deploys?
deploy-bot: deployed driver/gpu-runtime v520.61 to pool-prod-gpu-*. release: kernel selector heuristic tweak.
alejandro: ah thanks. perf numbers: baseline p50=12ms p99=38ms -> now p50=15ms p99=78ms for short seqs. long seqs unaffected.
taylor: can you dump last kernel choices from the tracer for a few requests?
alejandro: pasted a short sample from /var/log/runtime/traces.log (trimmed):
```
req_id=abc123 seq=8 batch=12 kernel=triton_gemm_v2 time_ms=1.92
req_id=abc124 seq=8 batch=12 kernel=triton_gemm_v2 time_ms=2.01
req_id=abc125 seq=32 batch=4 kernel=flash_attn_fast time_ms=0.88
req_id=abc126 seq=8 batch=12 kernel=triton_gemm_v2 time_ms=1.87
```
alejandro: we used to prefer flash_attn_fast for seq<=16 in 520.58. looks like the new selector now favors triton_gemm_v2 for those short sequences.
mei: that matches what I saw in the selector logs — the cost model weights got updated and the fallback penalty for kernel switch was lowered. small batches + seq8 now pick GEMM because it reports slightly lower theoretical FLOP cost, but in practice memory latency kills it.
rob: also seeing increased KV-cache allocator churn in the same timeframe, GC events up 3x. GEMM kernels allocate more temporary buffers that are 256B-aligned; that fragments our 64k slab pools.
dana: can you paste the allocator stats?
alejandro: allocator snapshot at 09:12 UTC: total_slabs=128 free_slabs=22 fragmented=16 eviction_count=184 reclaim_ms=420
alejandro: during the spike we saw eviction_count jump and per-request alloc latency up ~0.6ms. combine that with GEMM 2x kernel time and p99 blows up.
taylor: actionable options: 1) revert selector weight change in canary, 2) force flash_attn for seq<=16 as short-term pin, 3) adjust allocator alignment rounding to 128B to reduce fragmentation.
mei: I can push a canary config to pool-canary in 10m to test 2). recommend running nsys on canary to confirm kernel times under production load.
rob: also want a microbenchmark for GEMM vs flash on our small-batch seq8 with current driver — I suspect driver nvcc scheduling changed latency characteristics.
dana: timeline request: put a hold on global rollout until canary verifies. please include cost delta if flash_attn increases CPU or memory.
alejandro: starting canary: applying config override to force flash_attn_fast for seq<=16 on pool-canary. will roll back if no improvement in 15m.
infra-bot: canary config applied to pool-canary at 09:25 UTC by alejandro.
mei: started nsys profiling job (nsys job id 4521) capturing kernel wall times + memory ops.
alejandro: quick canary numbers after 7m: p99 for seq8 back to 41ms, p50=13ms. eviction_count down to baseline.
taylor: good signal. steps post-canary: 1) revert the selector change in next driver release candidate, 2) add a unit/regression test for short-sequence kernel choice using our cost model with live latency probes, 3) instrument allocator to expose slab fragmentation metric in console.
rob: I'll open a follow-up RFC to discuss allocator alignment and slab sizing; might be a quick win.
dana: please add an incident blameless postmortem with timeline and rollout decision. we need to mention the selector model drift and the allocator interaction.
alejandro: filing incident doc and RFC links in #incidents. for now keeping rollback paused until driver rollback is ready. thanks all :thumbsup:
